subject: geography
title: Urban Issues Adventure: Megacity Challenges
welcome_lead: Rapid urban growth brings squatter settlements, traffic, waste and water shortages. Let's see why.
meta_desc: GCSE Geography megacity challenges — slums, traffic, water, waste in NEE megacities.
final_note: You learned the social and environmental challenges of NEE megacities.

concepts.def: Informal housing on illegally occupied land
Too many vehicles for the road space
Unreliable access to safe drinking water

walkthroughs.body_html:
Growth outpaces formal housing. Migrants build their own — on swamps, hillsides, roadsides.

In Rio, around 20% of residents live in favelas like Rocinha.

Problems: no clean water, weak sewerage, fires, landslides, organised crime.

Rising incomes mean more cars but roads can't expand fast enough.

Mumbai commuters can spend over 90 minutes each way.

Air pollution from vehicles, generators and rubbish burning causes respiratory disease. Delhi regularly tops world pollution rankings.

Water: in Lagos, many residents have to buy water from tankers — far more expensive than mains supply.

Waste: official services miss informal areas; open dumps (Dharavi).

Work: huge informal economy — street vendors, rickshaw drivers, waste pickers — no tax, no rights.

Factory employee with a contract
Street vendor with no business permit

mcqs.q: Why do informal settlements develop in rapidly growing LIC cities?
options: People live in slums because they prefer them or are too lazy to find better housing.
It is the hole in the ozone layer letting in more sun.
Rural-urban migration outpaces formal housing supply; migrants build their own homes on marginal land without secure land tenure — driven by housing shortage, not by personal choice.
Informal settlements are built by the government for new migrants.
